title: Control plane orchestration roles — decision log and ownership rationale
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note captures the rationale and concise ownership map for the control plane components that make routing decisions in multi-region deployments. Focus is on three logical layers: API gateway (ingress/edge), orchestration (control plane decisioning, policies, rollouts), and runtime adapters (region-local adapters that translate control-plane intent into runtime actions).

Intended audience: platform engineers, runtime owners, SRE, and product stakeholders who are designing or integrating routing and fallback policies across regions.

Summary of decision statements (short):
- API Gateway: owns public ingress, auth, TLS termination, and coarse-grained region affinity. Must be simple and stable; not responsible for model-level rollout decisions.
- Orchestration layer (control plane): owns routing policies, model variant catalog, rollout logic (canary/A-B), global fallback rules, and quota accounting for cross-region policies.
- Runtime adapters: own the local execution surface, health signaling, local autoscaling triggers, and applying runtime-specific optimizations (quantization profile selection, kernel hints).

Why we split responsibilities this way (rationale):
- Separation of concerns reduces blast radius: edge can remain minimal and reliable; complex policy logic lives in orchestrator where we can version and audit it.
- Local runtimes must be able to act autonomously under degraded control-plane connectivity; that capability is essential for meeting regional SLOs.
- Centralized catalog + decentralized execution enables quick rollouts and consistent observability across environments (hosted/dedicated/private).

Concise ASCII ownership map (logical):

[Client] -> [API Gateway (edge)] -> [Orchestrator (control plane)] -> [Region Adapter] -> [Serving Runtime]

Responsibilities by component (detailed):
- API Gateway (Edge):
  - Tasks: TLS, auth, rate limit, client-facing metrics, coarse region routing (latency-based or geo-preference), initial header enrichment (x-region-hint), basic request shaping (max tokens override per plan).
  - NOT owned: model-level rollback, token-level billing reconciliation, runtime autoscaling knobs.
  - Owners: eng-platform-edge + eng-sre.

- Orchestration / Control Plane:
  - Tasks: policy store (routing policy DSL), model catalog and compatibility matrix, rollout engine (staged canary, weighted split), fallback policy engine (per-tenant, global), decision history (audit), quota/shaping coordination across regions, rollout-safety checks (quality/regression gating).
  - Exposes: decision API (sync) and async notification stream for adapters; audit log; simulated dry-run endpoints for product and SE to test changes.
  - Owners: eng-platform-orchestration (primary), eng-applied-ml (policy inputs), product for rollout definitions.

- Runtime Adapters (per-region):
  - Tasks: receive decisions, translate into runtime config (instance-to-model mapping, queue priorities), local health checks and metrics emission, autonomous fallback behavior if control plane unreachable, enforce local resource limits and pre-configured cache policies.
  - Runtime adapters must be lightweight and idempotent when replaying commands.
  - Owners: eng-serving-runtime (adapter code), local infra teams for region-specific infra.

Edge cases and failure modes we explicitly designed for:
1) Control plane unreachable (partial outage): adapters use last-known policy + pre-configured safety defaults. This includes max per-customer rate caps and sticky default model variant mapping.
2) Region isolation (network partition): API Gateway should be able to route to alternate region using orchestrator fallback hints; orchestration fallback may be disabled by tenant if they require strict data residency.
3) Upscale event where a region exhausts capacity: orchestrator signals burst policy to adapters and API Gateway can triage requests to lower-cost or higher-latency regions depending on tenant fallback policy.

Routing policy primitives (DSL sketch):
- match { tenant, model_family, request_latency, model_quality } -> action { region_preference: [pdx, iad, lon], variant_weight: {v1: 80, v2: 20}, fallback: {redirect, queue, reject}, ttl: 120s }
Notes: TTL on decisions allows adapters to cache for short windows; orchestration can push immediate invalidations when safety gates trip.

Decision log (chronological, condensed):
- 2025-03-11 — Initial proposal: single control plane with region-aware routing. Problems: too many edge responsibilities; risk of cold-starts on failover. (author: Marcus Chen)
- 2025-04-02 — Variant: push routing decisions entirely to edge. Rejected because it made edge too complex and slowed rollout velocity. (review: eng-sre, eng-platform)
- 2025-05-17 — Adopted hybrid: edge handles coarse routing and authorizations; orchestrator owns model-level rollouts & policy DSL. Approved with experimental canary in iad. (owner: Elena Torres)
- 2025-08-09 — Added requirement: adapters must operate independently for up to 15 minutes without control plane connectivity. Rationale: meet 99th percentile SLO during control-plane upgrades. (owner: Priya Nair)
- 2025-11-21 — Introduced tenant-level opt-out flag for cross-region fallback (compliance-driven). Requires explicit sign-off and opt-in for fallback otherwise. (owner: Alyssa Grant)

Operational runbook highlights (short):
- Deploying policy changes: use dry-run mode for 30 minutes against synthetic traffic; check quality metrics in console before enabling rollout.
- Emergency rollback: orchestrator exposes a kill-switch that sets all weighted policies to 100% stable variant and propagates invalidation to adapters. API Gateway will start blocking new model pulls for a short TTL to stop rollout.
- Observability: every routing decision gets a decision_id returned to the client and logged; correlates with token-level billing for cost analysis.

Multi-region considerations (practical guidance):
- Regional model pinning: for compliance, allow tenants to pin to specific regions; orchestrator must enforce pinning at policy-evaluation time.
- Geographic latency steering: edge should choose a preferred region by latency probe; orchestration can override for capacity reasons.
- Data egress: orchestrator must annotate decision with egress_cost_estimate and data_residency_tags. Billing tags should be emitted by adapters.

Open questions / trade-offs (to resolve):
- Should orchestration maintain soft-state placement suggestions (where to spin new runtime capacity) or should that be left to infra/autoscaler? Proposal: orchestrator emits placement hints but not direct autoscaling commands.
- How large should the TTL be on cached decisions? Current default 120s — tradeoff between responsiveness and control-plane load.
- Authentication model for decision API: mTLS + short-lived tokens vs signed JWTs. Prefer mTLS for adapters but need onboarding UX.

Action items and owners (next steps):
- (Elena) Draft API schema for decision API (v0) and publish by 2026-03-01.
- (Marcus) Implement dry-run harness that feeds synthetic traffic into orchestrator and adapters by 2026-03-15.
- (Priya) Define adapter autonomy spec (timeouts, retries, default fallbacks) and land as RFC by 2026-02-28.
- (Alyssa) Update compliance checklist to cover tenant opt-out lifecycle and auditing by 2026-03-10.

Quick references and links:
- Confluence page: PLT-architecture-overview (linked above)
- Jira epic: JIRA-PLT-987 (routing & orchestration)
- Proto for decision API: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/tree/decision-proto (PR linked above)

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally concise to act as an operational decision record rather than an exhaustive design doc. If you need the full system sequence diagrams and proto definitions, see the linked repository and the orchestration RFC drafts.

Unresolved: add a small appendix describing how Dedicated (reserved capacity) customers differ in their allowed control-plane interactions — they may require a local control-plane proxy; propose how that proxy syncs with the central orchestrator. (TODO: draft proxy sync model)

End of note.
